archetype: INT magician whose damage is concentrated in summoned Shikigami (Oni, Tengu, Orochi) rather than in her own direct attacks. IMPORTANT: this file describes the REMASTERED Kanna. Kanna was rebuilt in the GMS v266 update (The Sengoku Warrior Reawakening). The entire pre-remaster kit - Shikigami Haunting, Kishin Shoukan, Vanquisher's Charm, Nine-Tailed Fury, Spirit's Domain, Liberated Spirit Circle - no longer exists. Searching the current skill list on maplestorywiki returns zero occurrences of every one of those names. The current kit is built on Soul-Shatter Talisman, Heart-Wreck Talisman, the three Shikigami summons, and the four [Order] skills. Most Kanna material still ranking on the open web describes the deleted kit and will mislead a planner.

linkSkill.name: Elementalism
linkSkill.effect: Activating attack skills 40 times completes the preparation; the next attack skill use grants the Elementalism buff. At Master Level 3 the buff is Damage +20% for 12 seconds (Level 1 is Damage +10%). Grandis Library additionally records that the effect is unaffected by %Buff Duration.
linkSkill.levels: Master Level 3. Level 1 = Damage +10% / 12 sec. Level 3 = Damage +20% / 12 sec. The 40-attack activation requirement is the same at all levels. Level 2 value was not read directly and is left unstated rather than interpolated.

priority.node: Boost node / enhancement core groupings (which skills share a node). Core 1: Soul-Shatter Talisman Boost + Heart-Wreck Talisman Boost. Core 2: Summon Oni Boost. Core 3: Summon Tengu Boost. Core 4: Summon Orochi Boost. Core 5: [Order] Spinning Strike Boost + [Order] Pulverizing Strike Boost. Core 6: [Order] Shade-Fletched Arrow Boost + [Order] Execute Boost.
priority.why: This is the node-to-skill mapping, not a priority claim. It is the structural fact everything else rests on. Two independent sources give an identical grouping: the wiki's V Enhancements table (game data, no judgement attached) and Grandis Library's boost node block (class-doc lineage). RE-VERIFIED 2026-09-12: read the wiki's 'Boost Node/Enhancement Core 1..6' definition lists directly, and read Grandis's embedded page data, whose six-entry nodes array pairs the same skills. Independent agreement on all six cores.
priority.consensusReason: Two independent sources in exact agreement. Not labelled strong because the project rule reserves strong for 3+ independent sources; no third source publishes the core groupings.

priority.node: Grandis Library marks ALL SIX Kanna boost node cores as PRIMARY. It assigns no core to SECONDARY and none to OTHER.
priority.why: CORRECTED 2026-09-12. The previous version of this file said Grandis marked cores 1-4 PRIMARY and cores 5-6 SECONDARY. That is not what the page says. Grandis renders a sitewide legend on every class page defining three categories (PRIMARY = 'Boost Nodes that unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery and are skills that are frequently used'; SECONDARY = 'Boost Nodes that don't unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery but are still used'; OTHER = 'Boost Nodes that do not need to be upgraded or has least priority'). That legend is generic boilerplate, not a Kanna assignment. Kanna's own data assigns primary to every node index - the page's embedded data carries "primary":[0,1,2,3,4,5] against a six-entry node list - and all six rendered node blocks carry the identical tier colour. The legend's own wording explains why: all nine Kanna boost-node skills unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery, so by Grandis's definition none of them can fall below PRIMARY. The earlier claim read a generic legend as a Kanna-specific ranking.
priority.consensusReason: Single source (Grandis, which is class-doc lineage). No independent source tiers Kanna's boost nodes at all.

priority.node: Grandis Library DOES publish a ranked boost-node order for Kanna, in the form of three named trios: Primary Trio = Summon Oni + Summon Tengu + Summon Orochi; Secondary Trio = [Order] Pulverizing Strike + [Order] Execute + [Order] Shade-Fletched Arrow; Tertiary Trio = [Order] Spinning Strike + Soul-Shatter Talisman + Heart-Wreck Talisman. Its own guidance is to max the primary group first.
priority.why: CORRECTED 2026-09-12. The previous version said 'ordering WITHIN the primary tier is not established' and left it deliberately empty. That was wrong: Grandis's Recommended Nodes block ranks the three trios Primary / Secondary / Tertiary, and carries the note 'Any combination of these skills are good but preferred from same category as you want to max primary first'. So an order IS sourced - the three Shikigami summons first, then the three non-Spinning [Order] skills, then Spinning Strike plus the two Talismans. This is consistent with the independently sourced fact that Kanna's damage is summon-concentrated (see gearingNotes), which is why the summons lead. Caveat kept: this ranking is single-source and comes from the class-doc lineage, so it is a recommendation to compare against, not a settled fact.
priority.consensusReason: The RANKING is single-source (Grandis / class-doc lineage). mastermysty's Node Guide also publishes three Kanna trios but partitions the nine skills differently and states no ranking, so it does not corroborate the order.

priority.node: Per-node mechanical values, from the wiki's V Enhancement table (facts only). Final Damage: +2% per level on ALL NINE boost node skills. Level 20 effect: Critical Rate +5% on Summon Oni Boost, Summon Tengu Boost and Summon Orochi Boost; Normal Monster Damage +10% on the other SIX - Soul-Shatter Talisman Boost, Heart-Wreck Talisman Boost, [Order] Spinning Strike Boost, [Order] Pulverizing Strike Boost, [Order] Shade-Fletched Arrow Boost and [Order] Execute Boost. Level 40 effect: Ignored Enemy Defense +20% on ALL NINE, with no node distinguished.
priority.why: CORRECTED 2026-09-12 for two table-parsing errors. (1) The previous version said 'Soul-Shatter Talisman Boost gives Ignored Enemy Defense +20% at level 40' and that the level 40 column was only readable for that one node. The IED cell carries rowspan="9": it is a universal property of every Kanna boost node, not a distinguishing property of one. Treating it as distinguishing could push a planner to prioritise Soul-Shatter for IED, which would be a mistake. (2) The previous version listed four nodes with Normal Monster Damage +10% at level 20. The cell on the [Order] Pulverizing Strike row carries rowspan="3", covering Pulverizing Strike, Shade-Fletched Arrow and Execute, so the true count is six. Both errors were re-checked against the raw table markup. The crit half was already correct and is confirmed: Oni, Tengu and Orochi at +5% each, so those three nodes at level 20 are worth +15% Critical Rate in total. That summation is arithmetic on the source's figures, not a source claim.
priority.consensusReason: Single authoritative game-data source with no judgement involved, re-read at the raw-markup level so the rowspan structure is not in doubt. Not labelled strong only because the project rule requires 3+ independent sources.

priority.node: Mechanical constraint on trios: two boost nodes with the same Main Skill (the skill at the top of the node) cannot be equipped at the same time. Grandis states that six boost nodes in total are needed to reach Master Level 60 across these skills, with Matrix Points used.
priority.why: Recorded because it is the reason trio partitions exist at all, and because it constrains any ordering advice the product gives. Read from Grandis's Recommended Nodes notes.

vMatrix.notes: CORRECTED 2026-09-12 - the previous version of this field was wrong in both directions and has been replaced. It claimed 'NO post-remaster boost node trio recommendation could be sourced' and that mastermysty's Node Guide 'must NOT be used for Kanna' because 'its Kanna entry is built on Shikigami Haunting and Kishin Shoukan'. Both claims fail on inspection. (a) Grandis Library carries an explicit Recommended Nodes block for Kanna with three ranked trios - it was simply not read last time. (b) mastermysty's Kanna entry was re-fetched at the raw-HTML level: it contains zero occurrences of Kishin, Shikigami Haunting, Vanquisher, Nine-Tailed, Tengu Strike or Yosuzume, and its three trios name exactly the nine current post-remaster boost-node skills. The rejection also rested on a misread date: the page's only 'May 14th, 2024' belongs to a Monte Carlo line - '200 nodes: chance to find all trios. 10000 tests per class (May 14th, 2024)' - which dates a probability simulation, not the skill data. The page's own site stamp reads 'Last update: November 21st, 2024', which is itself stale relative to its post-remaster Kanna content, so the stamp is not a reliable guide to when the Kanna rows were written; the content is what was checked. Standing caveats for ingestion: mastermysty gives no ranking and no rationale, and its partition disagrees with Grandis's on two of three trios, so it is weak corroboration for one grouping and a genuine conflict on the other two - see conflicts.

hexa.notes: NO usable public source for Kanna HEXA investment order exists that could be read. This remains an honest null. What IS established and re-verified against the wiki on 2026-09-12: Skill Node/Core 1 (Origin) = [Divine Will] Advent of Crimson. Skill Node/Core 2 (Ascent) = [Divine Will] Final Rest. Nine Mastery cores, listed in masteryCores below. THREE HEXA Enhancement cores, listed in boostCores below. Why no order: Grandis Library carries no HEXA text section for any class - its Kanna page ships a '6th Job' infographic IMAGE (credited to lostara and brendon, dated 2026-06-25), which is a real lead but is not machine-readable and was not read here. The Kanna class doc that both maplestorywiki and Grandis still link is 'Post-6th Job Kanna Guide (Updated August 2024)', which is pre-remaster; its own text was re-read on 2026-09-12 and states verbatim 'i am done w/ updating the doc for a while so plz refer to kanna disc #faq for updated hexa max order', with a discord.com thread link. So the community's own answer explicitly lives in Discord, which is not publicly readable. Next step for whoever extends this: read the Grandis 6th Job infographic with OCR or a human, and pull the Kanna Discord #faq pins.
hexa.boostCoreNotes: CORRECTED 2026-09-12 - the previous version listed only one of these. The wiki's HEXA Enhancements section documents exactly three enhancement cores for Kanna, not one and not four. All three scale identically: Final Damage +11% at level 1 rising to +60% at level 30, with jumps at levels 10, 20 and 30 (+25% at 10, +40% at 20, +60% at 30). Master Level 30, level requirement 260. Each requires its corresponding V skill to be maxed and equipped. NOTE ON THE COUNT: Kanna has FOUR [Spirit] V skills - Hakumenkonmou Juubi, Unleash the Radiant Flame, Unleash Black-Winged Destruction, Unleash Soul-Searing Venom - but the wiki lists no enhancement core for [Spirit] Unleash the Radiant Flame. A count of four comes from conflating the four V skills with the enhancement cores; DigitalTQ's page makes exactly that conflation, labelling all four V skills 'Boost Skills'. Three is what the wiki's HEXA Enhancements table actually contains.
hexa.nameSourceNote: Origin, Ascent and all nine Mastery core names were re-verified against maplestorywiki and are independently reproduced name-for-name by DigitalTQ (https://www.digitaltq.com/maplestory-kanna-skill-build-guide). The three enhancement core names come from the wiki alone.

hyperStats.orderedNote: Empty and explicitly unordered. No source of any kind ranks or allocates Kanna hyper stats, so nothing here may be read positionally. Downstream code must not treat this array as a ranking.
hyperStats.notes: No Kanna-specific hyper stat allocation could be sourced. Re-confirmed 2026-09-12: Grandis Library's Kanna page contains zero occurrences of 'hyper stat' - it carries no hyper stat section for any class; the linked Kanna class doc is pre-remaster; DigitalTQ has no hyper stat content; NamuWiki's Kanna pages discuss inner ability but not hyper stat point allocation. Recording null rather than importing a generic cross-class list. Two things worth carrying into the product instead. (1) TOOL POINTER, NOT A CLAIM: the community's operative answer to hyper stat priority is a per-character computation from your own stat sheet rather than a fixed list, and MathBro's Hyper Stat Optimizer at https://brendonmay.github.io/hyperCalculator/ is the tool people use. (2) UNVERIFIED INFERENCE, EXPLICITLY NOT A RECOMMENDATION: Kanna runs short on Critical Rate (see gearingNotes, which IS sourced), so the Critical Rate hyper stat line is plausibly worth more to her than to a class that caps crit from passives. No source states this as a Kanna hyper stat recommendation. It is recorded as an inference to verify and must never be surfaced to a player as sourced advice.

hyperSkills.orderedNote: This is an unordered SET of five picks. Grandis presents it as three grouped lines, not a ranked sequence, so array position carries no meaning.
hyperSkills.consensusReason: DOWNGRADED from moderate on 2026-09-12. The wiki is cited alongside it only as a name-validation allowlist: it confirms all five picks are real hyper passives with those exact names, but the wiki makes no recommendation, so it cannot raise the source count for the selection.
hyperSkills.availablePool: Re-verified against the wiki 2026-09-12. Nine hyper passives, three for each of the three boosted skills: Pulverizing Strike - Reinforce / Critical Chance / Guardbreak; Shade-Fletched Arrow - Reinforce / Critical Chance / Boss Rush; Execute - Reinforce / Critical Chance / Guardbreak. The recommended build above takes five of these nine, which is the standard number of hyper passive points.
hyperSkills.actives: The wiki lists three hyper actives: True Name Revelation, [Order] Pulverizing Strike, and Akatsuki Blessing. Re-verified 2026-09-12. NO source recommends which hyper actives to take for Kanna - Grandis publishes a Hyper Skill Passive Build only and has no hyper active section - so no recommendation is given.
hyperSkills.notes: Grandis phrases its build as 'Pulverizing Strike - Reinforce and Guardbreak', 'Shade-Fletched Arrow - Reinforce and Boss Rush', 'Execute - Reinforce' - verified verbatim 2026-09-12. Two observations, both flagged as derived rather than sourced. (1) The three Critical Chance lines are available but not in the recommended build, which is worth flagging given Kanna's crit shortfall; no source explains that choice. (2) One of the three hyper actives, [Order] Pulverizing Strike, is the very skill that two of the recommended passives boost - the wiki's own description of Pulverizing Strike - Reinforce is 'Increases damage of [Order] Pulverizing Strike'. That is a structural reading of the wiki's data, not a recommendation any source makes.

Line 2/3: Boss Damage (Grandis states +10%; NamuWiki states a 5-10% legendary range; DigitalTQ states 20%)
Line 2/3: Damage to monsters inflicted with Abnormal Status (Grandis states +8%; NamuWiki states a 7-8% legendary range)

Per-line labelling, because the lines are not equally sourced. Boss Damage on lines 2-3: STRONG, named by three independent sources - Grandis (+10%), NamuWiki ('take it on the second-to-third line'), DigitalTQ ('20% Boss Damage'). Abnormal-Status damage on lines 2-3: MODERATE, two independent sources - Grandis (+8%) and NamuWiki ('used together with boss damage to maximise damage; take it on the second-to-third line', 7-8%). training.consensusReason: Single source (Grandis Library, class-doc lineage), re-verified verbatim 2026-09-12. It is also the generic training preset shape the cross-class inner ability guidance gives, so it is unlikely to be wrong, but nothing Kanna-specific confirms it.

innerAbility.classSpecificReasoning: NamuWiki gives the only readable reasoning for WHY Kanna's first line is contested, and it is worth encoding because it is a genuine post-remaster change. Re-read in the Korean original 2026-09-12 and confirmed on all four points. Its position: after the remaster, taking Passive Skills +1 is a meaningful damage gain because Kanna's damage is overwhelmingly summon-based and the passive levels feed that, whereas before the remaster the passive line was optional in GMS - it says passive is what people recommend nowadays precisely because Kanna's own average damage is overwhelmingly behind her summons'. Separately it notes that after the remaster attack speed reaches 7 stages, so in GMS an Attack Speed +1 roll is what lets a Kanna reach full attack speed - meaning the two line-1 candidates are solving different problems, and it says players nonetheless tend to favour the passive line. It also notes Critical Rate as a stopgap for players who cannot yet source crit elsewhere in the early-to-mid game, and says artifacts usually make that unnecessary later. A fourth line it mentions and this file does not recommend: Magic ATT, which it places on lines 2-3 as strictly worse than the Boss Damage plus Abnormal-Status pairing, calling that pairing effectively the endgame combination.
innerAbility.reasoningSourceNote: The English mirror at en.namu.wiki returned HTTP 403 on 2026-09-12, so the Korean original was read instead. Mirror and original are one source and count once. The 7-stage attack speed figure is independently corroborated by Grandis, whose Kanna attack stats block lists Attack Speed 7 (Stage 4 base, +2 from Peacock's Plumage, +1 from Kasen).

gearingNotes: Two Kanna-specific facts change gearing advice, both independently sourced and both re-verified 2026-09-12. (1) CRITICAL RATE SHORTFALL: NamuWiki states plainly that Kanna is very short on Critical Rate. This matters because it inverts the advice you would give a class that caps crit from its own passives - Kanna needs crit sourced from gear, Legion, artifacts, hyper stats or a stopgap inner ability line, and NamuWiki specifically suggests an inner ability crit roll as an early-to-mid-game patch until artifacts cover it. This dovetails with a mechanical fact from the wiki: the three Shikigami summon boost nodes (Oni, Tengu, Orochi) each grant Critical Rate +5% at node level 20, so those three nodes at level 20 are themselves worth +15% crit - i.e. for Kanna the boost node plan and the crit-rate plan are the same plan, and Grandis independently ranks exactly those three as the Primary Trio. (2) DAMAGE IS IN THE SUMMONS: NamuWiki states that post-remaster Kanna's own average damage lags well behind her summons'. That is why the summon nodes lead Grandis's trio order and why the Passive Skills +1 inner ability line gained value after the remaster. (3) ATTACK SPEED: NamuWiki notes that after the remaster attack speed sits at 7 stages - corroborated by Grandis's attack stats block, which also lists 7 - so in GMS an Attack Speed +1 inner ability roll is what reaches full attack speed, relevant to whether you chase that line or the passive line. Nothing was sourced on weapon/secondary/emblem selection, flame targets, or IED targets for Kanna, so those fields are absent rather than guessed. Note that Ignored Enemy Defense +20% arrives at node level 40 on every Kanna boost node equally and so is not a reason to prefer any particular node.
farmingNotes: DIRECT CORRECTION TO A COMMON ASSUMPTION, AND TO THIS TASK'S OWN PREMISE. Kishin Shoukan no longer exists on Kanna. Three independent checks agree: the wiki's complete current Kanna skill list contains zero occurrences of 'Kishin' across all job tiers, hyper, V and HEXA sections; Grandis Library's full active-skill list for Kanna contains no Kishin entry; and both NamuWiki Kanna pages contain zero occurrences. The pre-remaster kit that Kishin belonged to was removed wholesale in the v266 remaster. Caveat on strength: this is three sources independently showing ABSENCE from current skill listings, which is strong, but no official Nexon patch note saying 'Kishin Shoukan was removed' was read - Nexon's site is JavaScript-rendered and returned no content. A secondary, WEAKER claim from a low-quality source (DigitalTQ) holds that even before the remaster, GMS had already stripped Kishin's monster-spawn-rate increase in v233 and left it as an EXP buff; that is single-sourced from a content farm and should be treated as unverified history, not as current mechanics. PRACTICAL UPSHOT: do not plan a Kanna around Kishin, do not plan her as a spawn-support mule for another character, and treat any guide that recommends a Kishin boost node as proof that the guide predates v266. What replaces it for farming was NOT sourced - the current kit does carry Normal Monster Damage +10% at level 20 on SIX of the nine boost nodes (corrected 2026-09-12 from an earlier miscount of four; see vMatrix) and the standard Sol Janus EXP passive, but no source ranks Kanna's current farming performance, so no claim is made.
commonMistakes: Using the 'Post-6th Job Kanna Guide (Updated August 2024)' Google Doc. It is still the doc linked from BOTH maplestorywiki's class-guide index AND Grandis Library, which makes it the first thing a player finds, and it is pre-remaster: re-read 2026-09-12, it still teaches Shikigami Haunting, Kishin Shoukan, Vanquisher's Charm, Nine-Tailed Fury, Tengu Strike and Yosuzume, none of which exist. Its 'Perfect Trios' section recommends a Shikigami Haunting / Kishin Shoukan / Vanquisher's Charm trio. Its own text says 'i am done w/ updating the doc for a while so plz refer to kanna disc #faq for updated hexa max order'.

Treating Grandis Library and the Kanna class doc as two agreeing sources. Grandis's credits block attributes its Hyper Passive Build, Inner Ability and Boost Nodes Build to 'Class Doc' - verified verbatim 2026-09-12 - so they are one source family, not two. This is the single most important sourcing caveat in this file, because almost every judgement claim here traces back to Grandis.
Expecting a Kishin-based farming or spawn-mule role from Kanna. See farmingNotes.
Assuming the Grandis Kanna page is current to v.271. Grandis carries a sitewide GMS Ver. 269 stamp, two patches behind the v.271 target.

Reading Grandis's PRIMARY/SECONDARY/OTHER legend as a Kanna-specific node ranking. It is sitewide boilerplate. Kanna's data marks all six cores PRIMARY; the actual Kanna-specific ranking lives in the separate Recommended Nodes trio block.

V Matrix boost nodes begin at 200 and HEXA at 260, so the node and HEXA sections are forward planning, not current actions.

conflicts.topic: Inner ability first line for bossing
conflicts.positionA: Passive Skills +1. Stated by Grandis Library as the first bossing line. NamuWiki independently supports this, reasoning that post-remaster the passive levels feed Kanna's summons, which carry most of her damage, and noting this became recommended after the remaster where it had previously been optional in GMS.
conflicts.positionB: Attack Speed +1. Stated by DigitalTQ as its single inner ability recommendation ('1+ Attack Speed / 20% Boss Damage'). NamuWiki also presents this as a legitimate first-line option and explains the mechanism: post-remaster attack speed sits at 7 stages, so in GMS an Attack Speed +1 roll is what reaches full attack speed.
conflicts.assessment: Not resolved here, and arguably not a true disagreement - NamuWiki presents BOTH as valid legendary first lines solving different problems, and says players tend to favour the passive line because Kanna's own damage is overwhelmingly behind her summons'. Recorded as contested rather than resolved by preference. Lines 2 and 3 are NOT contested: Boss Damage and Damage to monsters with Abnormal Status, agreed by both independent lanes.

conflicts.topic: How to partition the nine boost-node skills into trios
conflicts.positionA: Grandis Library: {Summon Oni, Summon Tengu, Summon Orochi} / {[Order] Pulverizing Strike, [Order] Execute, [Order] Shade-Fletched Arrow} / {[Order] Spinning Strike, Soul-Shatter Talisman, Heart-Wreck Talisman}, ranked Primary, Secondary, Tertiary in that order.
conflicts.positionB: mastermysty Node Guide: {Soul-Shatter Talisman, Summon Oni, [Order] Spinning Strike} / {Summon Tengu, Heart-Wreck Talisman, Summon Orochi} / {[Order] Pulverizing Strike, [Order] Shade-Fletched Arrow, [Order] Execute}, unranked.
conflicts.assessment: NEW CONFLICT recorded 2026-09-12, after both sources were re-read. They agree on exactly one trio - the Pulverizing Strike / Shade-Fletched Arrow / Execute group - and disagree on the other two. Only Grandis states an order. Neither publishes a rationale. The honest reading for the product: the shared trio is moderately supported as a grouping; Grandis's ordering is a weak single-source recommendation worth surfacing as such; mastermysty's alternative groupings should be offered as an alternative, not as a correction.

conflicts.positionA: Grandis states +10%. NamuWiki states a 5-10% legendary range.
conflicts.assessment: The LINE is strongly sourced; the NUMBER is not. Surface 'Boss Damage on line 2 or 3' and do not commit to a percentage.

Hyper stat allocation - no source of any kind found for Kanna. Grandis has no hyper stat section for any class; DigitalTQ and NamuWiki have none for Kanna.
Which hyper ACTIVES to select - the three are named but no source recommends among them.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm. A resolution pass then re-opened every cited page and settled each defect.
contest.resolutionScope: Endgame only, per product-owner instruction: vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats, innerAbility. Job 1-4 skill builds, damage coefficients, damage lines, job tiers and rotations were out of scope. This file contains no job 1-4 or coefficient content, so no defect fell out of scope.

resolved.defect: FACTUAL ERROR (rowspan misread). vMatrix.priority[3] said 'Soul-Shatter Talisman Boost gives Ignored Enemy Defense +20% at level 40' and that the level 40 column was only unambiguously readable for that node. The critic found the cell carries rowspan="9".
resolved.action: Re-fetched https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Kanna/Skills with curl and read the V Enhancements table markup directly. Confirmed: <td rowspan="9">Ignored Enemy Defense: +20%. It applies to all nine boost node skills. vMatrix.priority[3] rewritten to state IED +20% at level 40 on ALL NINE with no node distinguished, and gearingNotes given a closing sentence saying IED is therefore not a reason to prefer any node.

resolved.defect: FACTUAL ERROR (same cause). The file listed four nodes with Normal Monster Damage +10% at level 20; the cell on the [Order] Pulverizing Strike row carries rowspan="3", making it six. farmingNotes repeated the error.
resolved.section: vMatrix (and farmingNotes, which repeated the same disputed claim)
resolved.action: Confirmed from the raw markup: Normal Monster Damage +10% appears on Soul-Shatter, [Order] Spinning Strike and Heart-Wreck as individual cells, plus a rowspan="3" cell covering Pulverizing Strike, Shade-Fletched Arrow and Execute. Six, not four. vMatrix.priority[3] and farmingNotes both corrected. The crit half was re-checked and is correct as written: Oni, Tengu, Orochi at +5% each, +15% total.

resolved.defect: FALSE CLAIM ABOUT A SOURCE'S CONTENTS. The file rejected mastermysty's Node Guide twice - in vMatrix.notes and commonMistakes[1] - on the grounds that its Kanna entry is built on Shikigami Haunting and Kishin Shoukan. The critic found zero occurrences of any deleted skill and a fully post-remaster Kanna entry.
resolved.disposition: CORRECTED - the rejection was withdrawn and the source reinstated with caveats
resolved.action: Re-fetched https://mystyjl.github.io/reference/NodeGuide.html and read the Kanna block at raw-HTML level (lines 1987-2043). Confirmed the critic exactly: three trios naming the nine current skills, zero occurrences of Kishin / Shikigami Haunting / Vanquisher / Nine-Tailed / Tengu Strike / Yosuzume across the whole page. vMatrix.notes rewritten, commonMistakes[1] deleted and replaced with a narrower caution (do not read its trio numbering as a ranking), and the sources entry reclassified from REJECTED to USABLE WITH CAVEATS. Its three trios are now in vMatrix.trios, each labelled weak and unranked.

resolved.defect: The evidentiary basis for the mastermysty rejection was also misread - '2024-05-14' was described as the guide's self-reported data date, when it belongs to a Monte Carlo simulation note.
resolved.disposition: CONFIRMED (the critic is right) and CORRECTED
resolved.action: Verified on the page: the only May 14th, 2024 is in '200 nodes: chance to find all trios. 10000 tests per class(May 14th, 2024)'. The page's own site stamp is 'Last update: November 21st, 2024'. Both are now stated accurately, with the added observation that even the November stamp is stale relative to the page's post-remaster Kanna content, so neither date can be used to date the Kanna rows.

resolved.defect: OMISSION presented as completeness: hexa.boostCores listed 1 of the 4 HEXA enhancement cores, inside a section claiming the wiki was used as a complete name-validation allowlist.
resolved.disposition: CORRECTED, with a correction to the critic's own count
resolved.action: Read the wiki's HEXA Enhancements section in full. It documents THREE enhancement cores, not one and not four: [Spirit] Hakumenkonmou Juubi Boost, [Spirit] Unleash Black-Winged Destruction Boost, [Spirit] Unleash Soul-Searing Venom Boost, all scaling +11% to +60% Final Damage with jumps at 10/20/30. There is no enhancement core for the fourth [Spirit] V skill, Unleash the Radiant Flame. The count of four appears to come from conflating the four [Spirit] V skills with the enhancement cores - DigitalTQ's page makes exactly that conflation. hexa.boostCores now lists all three, with a note explaining the count.

resolved.defect: NEWLY FOUND during resolution, not in the critic's list. CITATION INVERSION in vMatrix.priority[1]: 'Grandis Library marks cores 1, 2, 3 and 4 as PRIMARY, and cores 5 and 6 as SECONDARY.'
resolved.action: Grandis's Kanna page data assigns primary to every node index - "primary":[0,1,2,3,4,5] against a six-entry node array - and all six rendered node blocks carry the identical tier colour. The PRIMARY/SECONDARY/OTHER text on the page is a sitewide legend printed on every class page, not a Kanna assignment; the previous version read boilerplate as a ranking. Rewritten to state that Grandis marks all six cores PRIMARY, with the legend's definition quoted to explain why (all nine Kanna boost-node skills unlock a 6th Job HEXA Mastery). A commonMistakes entry was added warning against the same misreading.

resolved.defect: NEWLY FOUND during resolution. vMatrix.priority[2] asserted that 'Ordering WITHIN the primary tier is not established' and that 'no other readable post-remaster source ranks them', and vMatrix.trios was empty with a note saying no trio recommendation could be sourced.
resolved.action: Grandis Library carries a Recommended Nodes block for Kanna with three explicitly ranked trios - Primary Trio (Oni, Tengu, Orochi), Secondary Trio (Pulverizing Strike, Execute, Shade-Fletched Arrow), Tertiary Trio (Spinning Strike, Soul-Shatter, Heart-Wreck) - plus the note 'Any combination of these skills are good but preferred from same category as you want to max primary first'. It had simply not been read. An ordering IS sourced. priority[2] rewritten to carry it, vMatrix.trios populated, and a vMatrix.trioOrdering block added with ordered:true and an explicit warning that the ordering is single-source. The Grandis mechanical note that nodes sharing a Main Skill cannot be equipped together, and that six boost nodes are needed to reach Master Level 60, was added as a fifth priority entry.

resolved.defect: NEWLY FOUND during resolution. hyperSkills consensus was labelled 'moderate' while its own text conceded the five picks come from a single source family, and it listed the wiki among its sources as though the wiki supported the selection.
resolved.action: Downgraded to weak with sourceCount 1. Grandis is the only source that recommends a build, and its credits attribute the Hyper Passive Build to 'Class Doc'. The wiki was moved out of the sources array into a separate nameValidationSource field, because it validates that the five names are real but makes no recommendation. The build itself was re-verified verbatim against Grandis and the nine-passive / three-active pool re-verified against the wiki; nothing was deleted.

resolved.defect: NEWLY FOUND during resolution. innerAbility.bossing was labelled 'strong on lines 2 and 3', but the project rule reserves strong for 3+ independent sources and only Boss Damage has three.
resolved.action: en.namu.wiki returned HTTP 403 on the resolution date, so the Korean original at namu.wiki was read instead and confirmed every NamuWiki-attributed claim in this file: the two legendary presets, the attack-speed-versus-passive reasoning, boss damage and abnormal-status damage on lines two-to-three, the crit rate shortfall and the crit stopgap advice. DigitalTQ's '1+ Attack Speed / 20% Boss Damage' was re-verified verbatim. Labels are now per-line: Boss Damage strong (3 independent), Abnormal-Status damage moderate (2 independent), line 1 contested. A magnitudeNote records that the three sources give three different Boss Damage percentages, so the line is sourced but the number is not, and a third conflicts entry was added for it. The source URL was switched to the Korean original with a note that mirror and original count as one source.

resolved.defect: NEWLY FOUND during resolution (shape risk, pattern 3). hyperStats.priority was an empty array with no flag, and innerAbility / hyperSkills arrays carried no statement about whether position implies rank.
resolved.action: Added an explicit ordered flag plus an orderedNote to every list-shaped endgame claim. hyperStats.priority: ordered false, sourceCount 0, consensus none, with a note forbidding positional reading. hyperSkills.passiveBuild: ordered false - Grandis presents a set of five, not a sequence. innerAbility.bossing: ordered false for lines 2/3, which the sources explicitly treat as interchangeable. innerAbility.training: ordered TRUE, because Grandis genuinely numbers its lines and says the meso/drop pair swaps between lines 1 and 2. vMatrix.trioOrdering: ordered true, because Grandis genuinely ranks it - with a caveat that it is single-source. The hyperStats inference about Critical Rate was kept but rewritten to be unmistakably labelled as an unverified inference that must never be surfaced as sourced advice.

clearedOnInspection: NO fabricated names. The critic fetched https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Kanna/Skills and checked every name the file emits. All real and correctly spelled: the 6 boost-node core groupings (exact match), all 9 hyper passives and 3 hyper actives (exact match, including the availablePool description), all 9 HEXA Mastery cores (exact match, same order), '[Divine Will] Advent of Crimson' and '[Divine Will] Final Rest' (the wiki labels them 'Skill Node/Core 1 (Origin)' and 'Skill Node/Core 2 (Ascent)'), and Elementalism (Master Level 3, Lv1 +10%/12s, Lv3 +20%/12s, 40 activations at all levels - the file's refusal to interpolate Level 2 is correct). Grandis Library independently confirmed the hyper passive build, both inner ability presets, the 'Class Doc' credits, the GMS Ver. 269 stamp, and Legion Boss Damage +1/2/3/5/6%. Kishin absence reproduces: on the live wiki page 'Kishin' = 0, 'Shikigami Haunting' = 0, 'Vanquisher' = 0, 'Nine-Tailed' = 0, "Spirit's Domain" = 0, 'Liberated Spirit' = 0. DigitalTQ independently confirms the v266 'Sengoku Warrior Reawakening' remaster and the new skill names. NOT re-litigated in the resolution pass, except where a name count was itself a defect (see the hexa.boostCores resolution).

The resolution pass additionally re-confirmed, rather than disturbed: the six boost-node core groupings against both the wiki and Grandis; the nine hyper passives and three hyper actives against the wiki; the nine HEXA Mastery cores, Origin and Ascent names against the wiki AND independently against DigitalTQ; Grandis's hyper passive build verbatim; both Grandis inner ability presets verbatim; the 'Class Doc' credits line verbatim; the GMS Ver. 269 stamp; and the class doc's own 'refer to kanna disc #faq for updated hexa max order' line verbatim.
